disclosure: Synthetic English narration over fresh Chromium capture of actual production interactions. Native passkey approval is not simulated. No transaction settlement is claimed.

scenes.text: Meet Zerant. Prove trust. Preserve privacy. Applications often collect a full identity when they only need one reliable fact. Zerant brings private credentials and explicit consent to the Zcash ecosystem, without making a wallet address your identity.

A Zerant account opens a private trust workspace. Passkeys provide account access; no browser wallet connection is required. Organizations issue credentials. Holders review verification requests. Zcash actions have their own payment boundary. This walkthrough uses the live application on Zcash testnet, with real stored product records.

Inside the vault, Privacy Builders Collective has issued a Contributor Eligibility credential. The holder can inspect its status and issuer without publishing a complete credential portfolio. The Zerant ID lets an organization deliver a credential to this account. It is separate from a payment address, a wallet balance, and transaction history. Receiving a credential does not approve its disclosure.

The rewards portal asks for one fact: contributor eligibility. Here the holder reviews who is asking, why, and the exact claim that would leave Zerant. Denial remains available. Approval applies to this request, never to the holder's entire portfolio.
The verifier receives the approved answer: Eligible. The source credential and unrelated wallet information stay outside this result.
Payout routing is separate. The holder shares a temporary, encrypted, shielded-capable testnet destination with one trusted organization. It expires and can be withdrawn.
Review the exact recipient, amount, and testnet before wallet handoff. This payment request does not move funds. An external Zcash wallet must approve spending.
The request inbox keeps consent visible. Each request has a purpose and an expiry. A previous approval is not blanket permission for the next request.

Organizations have scoped tools for credential types, issuance, team permissions, and lifecycle management. Here, the real issuer has delivered one active credential. Issuing trust never grants wallet authority.

On a smaller screen, grouped navigation keeps credentials, requests, payments, and organization tools within reach. The drawer opens and closes as part of the real application. Forms and private account content adapt to the narrow viewport.
Zerant lets an application ask for a fact, rather than a person's entire history. Payment preparation is not settlement. Prove trust. Preserve privacy.
